Thanks Mina — looping Procurement formally. Alicia, welcome. A few procurement items we need to evaluate before we can approve a no-PO onboarding exception:

1) W-9 (for US vendors) or tax certificate for your entity.
2) Sample invoice showing billing cadence and remit-to details.
3) Written confirmation of pilot maximum spend and end date (we prefer absolute caps).
4) Any reseller/subcontractor relationships or third-party data handling notes (if data export or integrations are involved).
5) If services touch customer data beyond test accounts, we need to know whether SmallVendor maintains SOC/ISO attestations — if not, limit pilot scope.

Procurement policy overview (short): software subscriptions typically require a PO. Exceptions can be granted for pilots <= $5k for up to 90 days with Procurement + Finance sign-off and the vendor on a temporary invoice-only intake. Approvals will include: Procurement (me) and Finance (Laura).

Please send the docs and a signed one-page pilot statement (example below) and I’ll route for approval.

Example pilot statement we need signed by your legal/ops contact:
"SmallVendor will provide a trial of its SaaS product to Redwood Inference limited to a maximum of $4,500 and for a period ending no later than 2026-09-30. SmallVendor understands this onboarding is invoice-only and agrees to provide tax & billing documentation prior to provisioning."

Once we receive those, I’ll aim to get Procurement/Finance decision in 48 hours.

Thanks,
